exposure: Maternal body positions (sacrum flexible: standing, walking; sacrum non-flexible: lying, sitting) in the last 24 hours before birth
cohort: The study included 105 nulliparous women with an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy.
finding: Women spent 80% of their time in sacrum non-flexible positions during the last 24 hours before childbirth, and more than 90% gave birth in these positions, with a higher rate of epidural analgesia observed in women spending more time in sacrum non-flexible positions.
